EXTRACTION ALTERNATIVES 
Westmoreland Resources will use the area strip method (described in Chapter 1) to mine the coal on the lease. This is the most practical mining method where coal beds lie close to the surface over large areas as on the Tract II and III leases. Other technological methods exist for mining. Established surface mining methods include contour (prohibited by Montana law), auger, open pit, and quarry mining. Underground methods include room and pillar and longwall mining. Each method is best adapted to certain geologic conditions.
The coal deposits on the Tract II and Tract III leases are relatively flat lying and close to the surface. The only feasible surface mining method is the area strip mining method, and it is highly unlikely that low overburden conditions and thick seams would permit mining by underground methods.
COAL TRANSPORTATION ALTERNATIVES
COAL SLURRY PIPELINE
Coal slurry pipelines have been used in several coal mining developments to transport crushed coal over long distances. The most noteworthy is the 275-mile-long Black Mesa pipeline constructed by Peabody Coal Company. Underground pipelines would be environmentally desirable, since (except for pumping and storage facilities), they are usually unobtrusive. The slurry pipeline has proven to be an efficient coal transporting mechanism, and electrical energy requirements for transport of the slurry are minimal.
